reviews.comment: She's a great professor, goes over examples in class that apply directly to the homework and exams. There's a quiz every week but they are never difficult and pad your grade before the exams. There's 2 exams and a final which she provides practice exams for that are very helpful. I think people blame there struggle with dfq on her for no reason.

Lectures are great. She makes her own unfilled notes, which she then fills out during lecture, making it very easy to follow along and understand the material. Homeworks are brutal with excessively long problems, but are basically a completion grade. Exams are 80% and are pretty difficult; study hard for them. Overall, would recommend as a prof.

Would definitely recommend to take her! Even though her lectures are sometimes slow, she explains the process of the problems very well and easy to apply and understand. Homework is just some video quizzes and chapter homework but never too much. Very structured and has plenty of resources for help, which she mentions through the semester.

Dr. Wang is an overall fine professor. Lectures are alright, and her accent doesn't get too much in the way of understanding. Two of the lowest assignments in each category are dropped, and the final exam grade, if higher than previous exams, replaces the lowest exam score.

Doesn't answer questions very well, doesn't explain things very well. Kind of confusing the way she posted assignments for the week. She definitely means well and is a very nice lady, she just has a specific way of doing things and won't change it up to help her students.

(Math 140) Very sweet and easy to reach out to, but some parts of the class were annoying. Weekly quizzes given with not much time. There was webassign HW but it was doable. She does take attendance and does not post the filled in notes, so it makes studying difficult. Overall not hard if you study for quizzes/exams & do her practice tests!!

She is super sweet! If you're rating her low, you just have a problem with Math 140. Yes, there is a decent amount of homework in the class; however, there will be the same amount of homework for each Math 140 class. She is super nice and will answer any questions you have. Math 140 is pretty easy if you have a good basis from high school.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her for math 140  she's very sweet and approachable - however, her teaching isn't for everyone - she has an accent that can be hard to pick up at times - lot of hw once you get to a certain point it's ridiculous and overwhelming - you get a random quiz here and there - and exams are difficult as her teaching is chopped and fast pace.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took her for 140. She's sweet and kind, but I had a hard time following/understanding her in lecture and I felt like she wasted a lot of time in class explaining questions multiple times for no reason. I don't think notes were reflective of quizzes or exams either. I don't think this course should have been as difficult as it was with her.
She was very transparent about the topics that would be tested. I had a great time in her diffeq and would highly recommend her.

(I took MATH 140 with her, it's not listed as an option here) She's easy to understand, accessible outside class, and a nice person. Any problems I had with this class were not her fault but rather just issues with the way MATH 140 is designed as a standardized course.
She teaches well and is clear about what is on exams. Highly recommend!

TAKE HER!! Her exams were just like practice and she gives you so much material to study and makes sure you are prepared for the exams. She truly does care about her students and is very approachable. I got an 89.5 and she gave me an A. TAKE HER!!!!!!

Tests are 80% of the class, 2 Midterms that are 22% each and a final worth 36%. Homework, quizzes, and pythons assignments were all completion grade and weren't too hard but only made up 20% of the class. I fell short of a C by just a couple points on the final. Final is also accumulative so I felt like the weight was kinda a crazy expectation.

Very kind and sweet prof. Homeworks were completion grades and quizzes were take-home. Exams were easier than homeworks and quizzes and she was generous with partial credit. She posted recordings of lectures. Exams weighted a lot though--each was 22% of the course grade and final was 36%, but I think this was pretty standard across diff eq profs.

Accent isn't that bad but she goes fast (it's a lot of material). She is very kind and will help, but you have to go to MLC often to do well. Quizzes are much harder than lectures so you have to use the textbook. Would recommend learning some calc beforehand because some units can get rough. If you study hard you'll do well.

Dr. Wang is an amazing professor. Her lectures might be hard to understand initially because of a slight accent but you will get used to it. Her HWs are very helpful and take-home quizzes are easy. She gives practice for exams. Do those and you will do great in the class. Highly recommend her.
Professor Wang gave great, clear lectures. Weekly homework and take-home quizzes, and the exams weren't too hard. Would highly recommend her.

Her accent can be difficult to understand at times, and she tends to go at a faster pace (the course is fast paced no matter what) and not explain key concepts because she thinks it's common sense. She would post practice material that would be helpful for exam preparation. She also posted all the notes in case you missed class. Very sweet woman!

Sweet, Easy to follow. Accent isn't even bad, don't listen to those people. Exams weren't difficult. She posts a lot of extra help like practice exams and work out videos for previous exams. Also does quick review of all exam concepts before exams. I haven't taken a calculus class before hers. She was great.

I can't imagine taking this course without any previous knowledge in calculus as her explanations of each concept is quite shallow. However, credit where credit is due, she is a kind professor and offers some extra credit on exams. I highly recommend going to the MLC every week if you are going to take this class and want to pass with a good grade.
If you have no calculus background, this class may be tricky. She cares for her students a lot but her thick accent makes it quite challenging to understand her.

Dr. Wang is a kind professor but she is not effective at teaching AT ALL. She has a thick accent making lectures really difficult to understand, not to mention she does not explain anything or go in too depth during lessons. There are weekly quizzes which are 10x harder than actual lecture. Go to MLC if you want to get a good grade.

Professor Wang is a  kind professor and is open to helping students during office hours and after class, however she is not an effective teacher. She underexplains concepts and then proceeds to give very hard quizzes each week, which are often much harder than the material taught in class. They felt like the hardest possible problem for the unit.

She explains concepts fairly well, but you will most likely need to study excessively outside of class in order to truly understand them. She does not go super in depth, but in all fairness there's just a lot of material to cover and not a lot of time. There are weekly quizzes that can boost your grade if you've been going to class.

I do not recommend taking this class if you have not taken a calculus class previously; she does not go in-depth on how she reached a solution.  2/3 tests were given extra credit, and she dropped the two lowest grades in each section (homework, attendance, and quizzes), but that's because most students were struggling.

She is really sweet and seems to genuinely care about her students. There is a weekly quiz that ranges from 2-4 questions and can really impact your grade, and the grades don't go in for sometimes weeks afterwards. It is difficult to know what your grade in the class is at any given moment because of how long grading takes. I studied 20+ hrs a week
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS OR PROFESSOR. She does not explain anything thoroughly and just reads from the notes key she has. Weekly quizzes that she makes as difficult as possible and tricks you into thinking they will all be group quizzes, THEY ARE NOT. Has no sympathy for her students and does nothing to help them.

This professor has a heavy heavy Chinese accent that is hard to understand and distracting. Reads from her notes only and takes no time to explain how she got to certain point.  She constantly leaves out important calculations or steps from her notes as well, assuming that everyone is on the same page and level as her. Class was halved by November.

This Class was unesseasrily hard. There are quizzes weekly with the hardest versions of the questions. She is kinda hard to understand and bad a lecturing. She does not explin how to do  the problem and continuously would skip steps without saying that she was so it would just cause confusion.

If you haven't taken calculus in highschool already, this class will most likely be hard for you. This is my first calculus class, and I have trouble keeping up within lecture. To pass I have to relearn the subject on my own using the provided textbook. Each week there is a quiz and the problems are long. Go to MLC!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you're not already good at math, avoid this prof. Is not very good at explaining concepts and thick accent makes it hard to understand.

She puts the most difficult problems on the quizzes instead of going over the basics she makes each problem as difficult as possible with only 3 questions. First exam was awful most of the points are multiple choice questions but you will need to get help at mlc because without prior knowledge you will fill lost.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For someone who has never taken calc, she explained nothing, nada, zilch. She expected everyone to already know everything about calculus and gave a quiz every single week. She seems to like to always trick you with quizzes with absurdly long problems instead of just focusing on testing the concepts we learn. I don't recommend it!!!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She goes way too fast in class and her accent makes it difficult to understand
Very good lectures, prepared me for exams. Notes available on teams and her website. Standard math course.

Very endearing prof. She gives simple and effective lectures. She is very clear about what specific concepts will be on the exams (this helps a LOT). Homeworks and quizzes are easy and are similar to the exams. Quizzes are usually take-home. She provides plenty of practice exams. Exams are very fair and reasonable. She cares about her students.

Some classes I learned a lot, some I did not learn anything. You can easily get an A in this class if you do the homework and quizzes and then use the practice exams and posted notes for each exam. The 3 exams (including final) are very heavily weighted and the hw//quizzes are easy 100s. If you study for the exams, you'll get an A. No curve/ex cred

Good at explaining concepts. Lectures notes are posted online and give good review.

She gives an unreasonable amount of hw in my opinion especially if you want to do them properly. She did not give practice exams for the final which I did not like. She gave practice exams for the two midterms. Overall a decent professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory but her lectures are important in understanding the material. She is excellent at explaining material that can be foreign to you at first. Her midterms can be too long to finish in 50 minutes. One thing I didn't like about her is that she made us do a quiz and 3 homework assignments on the week of finals.

Dr. Wang is a super nice professor and gives great lectures. Her accent can be a little difficult to get over at first, but it's not too bad. She gives homework from a textbook that's somewhat difficult, but all the answers are online. The weekly quizzes are pretty easy and even though the tests are hard, she's a really nice grader.

Professor Wang has good notes, but it sometimes hard to understand.  She spends wayyyyy too long going over proofs rather than actual problems.  She is very sweet and doesn't grade too hard.  She does assign homeworks and quizzes without warning and will make them due after two days.

She assigned a ridiculous amount of homework that would take hours and her tests were near impossible. She had a T/TH class and M/W/F class and I am pretty sure she did not change the tests because no one ever finished the tests on time in the mwf class. She would also do problems wrong in class. Seems to be good for cal one NOT diffeq.

she seems very nice, but moves very quickly in lectures. moves through problem steps so quickly that if you get lost or hung up on understanding any single part, she's done working on it by the time you catch up. homeworks assigned from textbook are often overly tedious for the quantity assigned.

I was referred to this professor by my Cal 3 prof. It was hard to get over her accent initially, but she really is a good professor. She is very sweet and kind and she wants you to do well. Her class is not hard, just do the homework and go to lecture. AND the week in reviews (these help reinforce everything).

Wang is a good professor and I enjoyed her class. There were quizzes in class but half the time we could use our partners. Exams weren't too difficult and I would study literally an hour before. An A is easily achievable I just didn't apply myself lol. Weekly homework assignments and some very easy 2 question videos every week.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was a really hard class but the professor herself wasn't bad. I had to go to the math learning center maybe 5-6 times which sucked but i eventually learned the material so that's what counts. The reason I had to receive help outside of class is because the homework is significantly harder than the example problems done in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such a nice caring professor who will understand your situations. Pretty standard work load for any A&M math class- homework and a quiz once a week, tests every few weeks. Challenging class but one of the better professors for MATH 142.

I'm not a math person and this was my first calculus class, so I was a little worried, but it was a lot easier than I expected. Lots of pop quizzes (she usually tells you before, but not always). Some are individual, some with notes, and some are group quizzes. She almost always gives partial credit. USE MLC WEEK IN REVIEW!

She was difficult to understand, and did not explain thoroughly, will just walk you through an example and use fill in the blank notes. Every time I tried to go to office hours she was not there or was late. The format of the class is great bc all lowest grades for every category will be dropped and final replaces lowest test grade. GO TO THE MLC!!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bless this girl, she was so nice - just takes things very fast. If you are not the best at math and need it explained well, I suggest taking from another professor.

Prof Wang is the sweetest of sweeties. She takes things slow in lecture and always asks her students if she can move on. Her quizzes are sometimes ridiculously more difficult than any practice problems we do, but she gives partial credit on them. If you don't already know some calculus you might need outside help. Take notes and pay attention!!!

Lectures consist only of example problems from the textbook, which are completed with little to no explanation of concepts or how to apply the example to other problems. Quiz questions are ridiculously hard compared to anything in the notes. If you've taken calculus before and done well, you should be fine, but if not, I would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had Math 142 with professor Wang which can be a challenging class, especially for people who are not the best at math. Professor Wang is a good teacher and is nice and understanding its just the course coordinator that makes Math 142 awful, but overall I would take her again.

Dr. Wang is a very helpful and caring professor. Concepts are mostly taught from online video modules and webassigns are due weekly. In class, she goes over practice problems and assigns weekly in-class quizzes which are either open-note or group work. She also posts practice exams with keys before every exam and gives extra/partial credit.

Dr. Wang was very hard to understand at times and the class is very dull. All she does in her lectures is read off the textbook and do the problems with little real explanation. The only reason I was able to get a B is due to the math learning center tutoring me and the TA being very available and helpful.

Kun Wang is a great choice for Diff EQ. I unfortunately did pretty poor on the final so I ended with a C, but that wasn't her fault in the slightest. She is kind, and will tell you before the exam the topics that you'll be tested on. Watch out for take home quizzes that'll be due Friday night. Would definitely take again

Overall professor Wang was good. Diff eq is a difficult course, but this professor made it easy. She let us know the what would be covered on the exams beforehand, which was very helpful. You'll be good if you do the hw, study for exams, and show up to class.
She used many examples in class so lectures were helpful for understanding what would be on tests. Graded fairly.

She is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Always willing to help you out. She tells you EXACTLY what is covered on the midterms and on the final. All you have to do is study those few selected topics for an easy A. She makes this class extremely easy.
Helpful and class is interesting.

I have learned a lot in my classes with Professor Wang. She is a very thoughtful teacher who puts a lot of thought into how she presents the material. She was very patient with everyone in the class and always encouraged her students to try. She helped me through this hard semester and I would highly recommend her!

I had taken pre-cal previously in highschool where I truly began to love math, yet when I came here to take pre-cal, it was so much harder than it needed to be with professor wang. The homework was very, VERY excessive and made it harder than it truly needed to be.

Dr. Wang is nice and very willing to help her students. However, differential equations will require a lot of work to do well. The homework is mandatory, but it is helpful. She uploads her lecture notes online, so you can access them if you miss class, but definitely try not to miss her lectures as it is easy to fall behind.

Kun was great! She is super sweet, but sometimes hard to understand. The diff-eq lectures could put me to sleep. The class is pretty much just tests and homework, and I'm not sure if it was her or the TAs, but they were a little stingy with partial credit. There was a lot of homework, but not as much as other profs. She rounded my 89 to an A!

I honestly could have done better in the class if I would have paid more attention to the material. The first exam was a few questions. All open-ended. The second exam was split into two parts which made the exam bearable. The final exam had-multiple choice and free response. Had lots of HW. she started to have pop quizzes after lectures so beware!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Class is pretty straightforward, study the review she gives you and practice hw and you're good to go. Solid professor, pretty cute too, I would recommend.
Everything she teaches is clear and concise. She also pushes back homework if she feels like she hasn't covered the material well enough thus far. Really nice too!

One of the strangest classes I've ever taken. Took 150 with her last semester, stopped showing up for the lectures after week 1. Can barely understand her, takes getting used too.. Below average class. First three exams are insanely easy, be warned though because the final is crazy difficult, I got a 58 and ran off with a B. Find someone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Wang had such a heavy accent that it was really hard to pay attention and learn anything in that class. Mainly had to teach myself the material. Homework is a big part of the grades so if you're not on top of that then you won't do well. Tests were ok just make sure you practice her examples she gives in her notes.

I really didn't like this prof. She was an okay lady but she was honestly really hard to understand. I didn't go to class half of the time because the lectures didn't explain or help anything. All she did was write down the answer to the problem and not explain wht she was doin. I would usually look at other professor's notes to study for a class.

Honestly, my high school pre-cal teacher taught me better. Hard to understand because thick accent, but sweet professor. Went to her office hours once for help on hw and she was fairly helpful. Attendance wasn't mandatory but towards the end of the semester she noticed people stopped coming to class & took attendance for extra credit.

I took precal in HS, so this definitely helped me in MATH150. Wang is an OK prof. She is very sweet but can be very difficult to understand. Since she puts the filled in notes online, I stopped going to her class because all it did was confuse me. I was still able to get high A's on tests by going over HW and reviews a few days before.

Dr. Wang is a good professor if you really put in your work. Her accent is a bit hard to understand, but most professors have accents, so as long as you pay attention to her class, you will be fine. Even if you couldn't understand her work, ask her in/out class and there's also filled uploaded notes. Anyway, attention in her class is the key.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: MATH151 is not an easy class. I had Calculus AB in high school and got a 100, and I struggled. She assumes you have a strong calculus background, and explains some things in a very complicated way when there are much easier ways to explain it. She is very sweet though, and is very helpful and understanding.

Dr. Wang was awesome! Her accent is a little hard to understand at first but don't let that derail you. If you take notes along with her it's super easy to follow the material. She even posts the notes she completed in class on her website. She curved our tests and is giving us extra points for each time we showed up to her lectures, so don't skip.

She is a pretty good prof. She mostly does practice problem and sometimes doesn't fully explain each step she takes but she still is very good. She puts her worksheets online to print out and bring to class then she uploaded the worksheet filled out. Her test weren't bad just half multiple choice and half work out. She was very generous with points

Dr. Wang was such a sweet and kind professor! She was always willing to help if you are confused, but her accent can sometimes be a bit hard to understand. Tests are generally easy, with half MC and half free response. The examples done in class are almost mirrored on homework or exams, so definitely show up! Tests are usually curved too!

She was a very sweet and really adorable professor, there was quite a bit of online homework through WebAssign but nothing too overwhelming. Her accent is a bit hard to understand sometimes, but as long as you are engaged in her lectures you'll do fine. She curves most of the exams and makes test reviews that are almost EXACTLY like the test.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not bad, but also not the best. Sometimes it seems like she doesn't know what she's talking about. Students correct her often. Hard to catch up if you miss class. She is very kind though.
The professor's tests are way more difficult than need be, with some questions appearing out of nowhere.

Her teaching style goes well with those who are consistent with attendance. Her lectures are clear and she answers all the questions you have. One complaint is that the notes she posts online are really bland and useless for the most part. The tests are pretty hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kun Wang is a great prof. She gives detailed lectures and cares about the students' learning, using a mic to make sure she reaches everyone. Exams are not too bad as long as you study, and she posts helpful test reviews and her notes online.

Kun Wang is a great prof, she teaches well and her tests are wholesome and not super difficult(at least for math 150). as long as you pay attention in class or read the book you will be fine. I am writing this review right now because i slept in and was 45 mins for the test. she kindly let me take it with her next class 30 minutes later. love her

Kun Wang is a good teacher. She's very quiet but uses a mic so you can hear over the annoying girls who talk the whole class. All her slides are online so you can look over them after class. She offers extra credit every now and then.
